threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still believe the bus will come on time. Watch the locals flinch at the first 'expected arrival'.
Caught a natter between two guys on the 45 last night. One swore he saw a ghost at the old cinema. Brixton’s stories never sleep.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: You know you’re in Neukölln when the café on the corner runs out of croissants because the baker’s cat decided to nap on the delivery truck.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a Späti selling vegan döner that doubles as an art gallery after dark. Totally unique vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they still grumble about the BART delays like it’s a rite of passage, not just another commute hassle.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy pull out a full-size piano on the corner of Eddy and Jones, played a magical tune as the 19 bus rolled by. Only in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals use them to catch up over vermut and tapas, not just for the scenery.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order a café con leche—only the locals know it’s a morning drink, not an afternoon treat.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can tell a newbie by the way they stare at the 38 bus schedule—no one around here waits for it anymore.
Caught a guy serenading a stray cat on the N109 last night. Cat seemed unimpressed, but the audience of two was rapt. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The mix of Turkish bakeries and hipster cafés on every corner, with the smell of fresh simit wafting through the air—only here do both worlds collide so deliciously.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a Kombucha café next to a punk rock bar, both open until 2 AM. It's the only place where health and chaos coexist so seamlessly.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows to dodge the BART announcements like a pro—those distractions won't save you from being late to dinner.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where the driver sang along to oldies. Hilarious distraction as 10 people were crammed in like sardines.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all vermut bars are the same, but locals know the hidden gems where the cat sits on the counter and the owner remembers your drink.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival in Gràcia by the way they still buy bottled water from the corner shop, oblivious to the sweet taste of tap water here.
